name: Pugilis
_grid: One character per tile, row 0 = the far side (player 2), last row = player 1's side. Each character is defined in the legend.
_legend: level = height step (0 = lowest); tiles interact only within 1 level. The middle stair pairs (V) have wedges on their own tiles rising from the landing to the floor on every floor side, meeting in mitres (slant = their width, 0.559: 60 degrees; rise: true; sheer: true = the drop to the pit stays a wall; shade: false = plain sand). The corner stairs (s) are plain blocks. (The user's choice, 2026-11-22, after trying many stair designs.) surface picks the look from the palette. marker = something on the tile (painted on the board, and for flags/bells a 3D piece from tools/place_pieces.py). paint: false = don't paint the marker. orient: away-from-pit = turn the painted marker so its bottom points away from the neighbouring lower tiles. piece: true = also put a 3D piece there (tools/place_pieces.py: flags, bells).
_edges: Marked tile edges: [row, col, side N/E/S/W]. fall = taking damage next to this edge knocks a Pokemon into the pit.
_board: The published board files the map picker uses (from tools/build_board.py; update when a new version is published), then run tools/build_arena_index.py.
_stair_lines: No step lines painted on the stairs (the user's choice, 2026-11-22).
_table: Image for the table around the board: the user's Dirt 2 / Dirt 5 mixed like the top floor, a shade darker (between the top floor and the stairs; tools/draw_placeholders.py pugilis_table).
_textures: Image textures for surfaces (paths relative to this folder; images = pick one at random per copy). span = tiles one copy covers; vary = random quarter-turns and mirrors per copy; match = recolour to the surface's palette colour (or a named palette entry). walls = the inner walls (where ground drops inside the board); outer = the board's outer edge too. walls:<surface> = that surface's inner walls get their own image (tools/wall_texture.py previews and publishes them): the user's cliff art, Cliff 6 on the ground floor's walls and Cliff 8 on the steps' sides, both fitted from the pit floor (level 0) up to the ground floor (level 2) so the layers line up; above: floor = the steps' walls show the ground floor's cliff above the step's top and under the middle stairs' wedges; vary mirror = copies flipped at random.
